conclusion: Erdos #126 is not settleable at scout cost and the scout died on a pre-registered kill condition (suggestive finite data, no iterable lemma, no exp(o(k)) reduction). Two things survive: the positivity mismatch is resolved (f(n-1) <= f0(n) <= f(n), so the Formal Conjectures Finset Nat statement is faithful for the limit and wrong for pinned finite values, f(2)=1 vs f0(2)=0), and arm 3 points the wrong way -- a rigorous composition law would refute the conjecture rather than prove it, since g(1)=2 plus supermultiplicativity gives g(k) >= 2^k by Fekete.
confidence: High on the two survivors and low on everything numeric. The positivity inequality is a four-line proof, checked independently by exhaustive subset search over [0,40]. The Fekete direction argument is elementary and self-contained. The g(k) table is exact only inside a bounded universe: every value is a rigorous LOWER bound on g(k) with a re-verified witness, no upper bound on g(k) is established anywhere, and seven points of a monotonically falling k-th root cannot distinguish a limit of 1 from a limit of 1.3. Do not let anyone read the table as evidence for or against the conjecture.

core_candidates.what: An 'inverse the extremal function before running the arms' step in the brief template: when a brief asks for an asymptotic bound on a minimum over unbounded sets, first state the inverse staircase and restate the conjecture as its growth rate.
core_candidates.why_reusable: Doing this once turned three unrelated-sounding arms (p-adic pruning, S-unit cliques, composition gadgets) into three measurements of one integer sequence g(k), made them directly comparable, and exposed within minutes that arm 3 was a refutation search rather than a proof route. That last point would not have been visible from the original formulation and would have consumed the whole budget.
core_candidates.first_step: Add one line to the brief generator's prize-scout template: 'if the target is an asymptotic bound on an extremal function, name its inverse and state the conjecture as a growth rate before allocating arms.'

core_candidates.what: A direction check on any proposed promotion criterion: before funding a search for a structure X, ask what X being found would prove.
core_candidates.why_reusable: This brief listed 'a rigorous composition law' as a promotion criterion, and a composition law here refutes the conjecture. A cheap explicit check catches promotion criteria that point away from the goal, which is a class of mispricing no amount of compute recovers from.
core_candidates.first_step: In the brief generator, require each promotion criterion to carry a one-line 'what it would establish, and in which direction' field, and refuse a criterion that leaves it blank.
